newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Sept 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Sept 18.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- RAIL GROUP CHIEFS NET 6 MILLION POUNDS IN SHARES

Prism Rail, the fledgling train operator, will grant four directors and six founder shareholders shares totalling up to 6 million pounds stg after winning the franchises for South Wales and West and Cardiff Railways yesterday. Prism, set up by bus company executives specifically to bid for rail operators, won a joint bid for the two seven-and-a-half year franchises and will be given government subsidies of 90.8 million pounds stg for the first year, declining to 51.4 million pounds stg in 2003.
-- GRANADA LIFTS STAKE IN YORKSHIRE TV

Granada, the media company, yesterday increased its stake in Yorkshire Tyne Tees TV to 27 percent and fuelled speculation that it is considering an imminent takeover of the ITV broadcaster. Granada announced it had exercised warrants in Yorkshire yesterday after the market closed, which left it sitting on a profit of 19 million pounds stg.
-- LEGAL MOVE BY BALTIC EXCHANGE

The Baltic Exchange, the shipping group, may take legal action against English Heritage and the City Corporation if the proposed redevelopment of the group's headquarters gets the go ahead. Trafalgar House, the property company that bought the site from the Exchange last year, has discussed offering at least 10 million pounds stg if English Heritage releases if from requirements to restore the listed property, bombed in 1992 by the IRA. The Exchange had to sell the St Mary Axe property for just 10 million pounds stg because of the cost of restoration.
THE TIMES
-- SEARS PLANS UP TO FOUR MORE SELFRIDGES

Troubled retailer Sears is to open up to four more regional Selfridges department stores, as well as a new development in Manchester and the extension to the Oxford Street store. The move is to capture the middle-class shopper with the new stores being in city centres with large catchment areas.
-- TESCO PULLS OFF SALES AND PROFIT SPECTACULAR

Tesco yesterday reported pre-tax profits up by 10.7 percent to 321 million pounds stg in the 24 weeks to August 10, despite the petrol price war that is estimated to have cost it 20 million pounds stg. The companies like-for-like sales in the UK grew by 7 percent, and volumes by 3 percent. One analyst described the performance as 'pretty spectacular'. Despite the news, Tesco's shares fell 5.5p to 297p as the City worried about the impact of its 'unbeatable price' promotion launched last week.
-- BRITISH AIRWAYS JOB LOSSES LIKELY TO BE LIMITED TO 5,000

British Airways chief executive, Robert Ayling, will tell a meeting of managers at Heathrow today that the final figure of job losses due to the radical shake-up of the airline could be about 5,000. Staff had feared that up to 10,000 jobs could be lost in the reorganisation of the airline over the next three years. Mr Ayling will also outline his vision for the transformation that he claims is essential if BA is to compete in the fast-changing international marketplace.
THE GUARDIAN
-- ALARM AT PDFM MARKET GAMBLE

Tony Dye, who controls 50 billion pounds stg at PDFM, Britain's second largest pensions manager, is expected to defend his strategies from accusations that he has gambled huge sums against a rally in worldwide stockmarkets 18 months too early. Some rival fund managers are saying that Mr Dye's reputation depends on a stock market crash before the year end.
-- DEBT BLOW TO CLARKE'S TAX CUT HOPES

Official figures showing public finances were 4.5 billion pounds stg in the red last month have put pressure on the Chancellor of the Exchequer, Kenneth Clarke, to leave tax levels on hold in the Budget. Despite the increase in Public Sector Borrowing Requirement, it is thought that the pressure to reduce personal tax levels in the run up to the general election may be too strong to resist. Business lenders are calling on the Chancellor to leave tax levels alone.
-- OLIVETTI CRISIS DEEPENS AS INQUIRY TARGETS DE BENEDETTI

The former chairman of Olivetti, Carlo De Benedetti, has been placed under judicial investigation for his role in events leading up to the publication of the company's interim results earlier this month. Magistrates have also targeted the man who replaced Mr De Benedetti as chairman, Antonio Tesone, and the company's former general manager Corrado Ariaudo.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- OFT TO CURB BA-AMERICAN DEAL

The proposed alliance between British Airways and American Airlines is to have curbs imposed by the Office of Fair Trading. The curbs will cover six key areas of the deal as a condition for allowing it to proceed without a monopolies referral. The OFT is expected to submit its formal recommendation to the President of the Board of Trade, Ian Lang after a meeting of the Mergers Panel next Monday.
-- ALLIANCE PLANS TO ACQUIRE MUTUAL LIFE FIRM NEXT YEAR

Alliance & Leicester has plans to build itself into a key financial services player by taking over a mutual life company after its stock market flotation next year. The building society has held talks with likely targets but has not yet narrowed down a shortlist. Its ambitions were revealed as it reported operating profits of 192 million pounds stg for the first six months of 1996, up 18 percent on the same period last year.
-- P&O PREDICTS CHANNEL CUTBACKS

Chairman of shipping to property conglomerate P&O, Lord Sterling, predicted yesterday that cross-Channel ferry capacity could be cut by up to one-third over the next year with fares rising following the government's decision to allow rival operators to forge closer ties. He confirmed that P&O are in discussion with the main ferry companies, who are open to finding solutions to the price war that has broken out since the start up of the Channel tunnel.
